title: A monitor's picture was recoverable from its radio leakage
body: In 1985 Wim van Eck demonstrated reconstructing a CRT screen's image from its unintended electromagnetic emissions at a distance, with cheap equipment. Intelligence services had whispered about such leakage, codename TEMPEST, for decades. The paper dragged the phenomenon into public, and shielded-room standards followed. Computers broadcast their work in more spectra than the intended one.
source_hint: van Eck (1985), 'Electromagnetic Radiation from Video Display Units'
